reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full RequestGroup StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level judgment, direct behavior findings in SearchParameters and HttpRestBehavior whose affectedResources include RequestGroup, and shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context as non-scoring background. I also checked the local R4/R6 package definitions for the resource identity and key element shapes.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 RequestGroup is trial-use/FMM 2, so the stability burden is neutral rather than normative. That softens the case for preserving every old path, but it does not erase the high operational impact of a resource-type replacement in CDS/workflow orchestration.

overall.oneLineConclusion: RequestGroup is effectively replaced by RequestOrchestration, so a migration program is unavoidable, but low-cost aliases and transition guidance still matter.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a mostly stable same-resource version bump. The R6 ballot package has no `StructureDefinition-RequestGroup.json`, does define `RequestOrchestration`, and lists `RequestGroup` in `fhir-old-types`; raw R4 instances, parser dispatch, generated model names, canonical profile references, REST endpoints, and search surfaces therefore need an explicit RequestGroup-to-RequestOrchestration migration. Once that is accepted, many child-element differences are local transform work, but not all compatibility preservation loses value.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The dominant shape is a removed/replaced resource plus targeted remodels inside the successor. Key required transforms include changing the resource identity, merging `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` into `reason` CodeableReference, wrapping `action.participant` references under the R6 participant actor model, and renaming `action.relatedAction.actionId` to `targetId`. R6 also adds optional orchestration capabilities such as goals, definitions, input/output, location, dynamic values, transforms, and relative timing that mostly affect R6-to-R4 retention policy rather than old R4 validation.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A resource-level migration program is already unavoidable, so preserving each child path is less valuable than providing a clear top-level migration map. However, that is not the same as saying extra breaks do not matter. Low-cost preservation is still valuable for same-semantics renames such as `relatedAction.actionId`, for endpoint/search transition behavior, and for explicit documentation or aliases that help generic clients discover the replacement. Richer remodels such as CodeableReference reasons and participant backbones look more like proportionate local migration chores.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy less-breaking alternatives are preserving `RequestGroup` as a deprecated compatibility identity or documented alias, keeping `relatedAction.actionId` as the wire name while clarifying its meaning, and documenting or aliasing common retired RequestGroup search/API surfaces. Less-breaking alternatives for `reason` and `participant` are only partial because they would duplicate the new R6 representations and require conflict, ordering, and precedence rules. Optional R6-only additions are not R4-to-R6 breaks and should be handled by conversion policy rather than by constraining R6 expressivity.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings reinforce the resource-level conclusion. `RequestGroup?patient` and other RequestGroup-based searches disappear with the removed resource base, and the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises a RequestGroup REST endpoint. These are real API migration concerns, but they are derivative of the resource identity decision. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search changes were treated as context only because RequestGroup is neither Resource nor DomainResource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that the resource shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource` and that major migration is `Yes`. I differ slightly on leverage: the resource migration dominates planning, but the best resource-level posture is not to dismiss additional compatibility work. Preserving or documenting low-cost aliases and transition behavior remains useful even though it cannot avoid the broader migration program.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for computable R4/R6 package differences and direct behavior report linkage. The remaining uncertainty is official intent and transition policy: no official migration ConceptMap, rendered change notes, or ballot rationale was supplied for RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration.

findingConsiderations.title: RequestGroup is absent in R6 and appears replaced by RequestOrchestration
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive break. R4 has a concrete `RequestGroup` resource while the R6 package has `RequestOrchestration` and no same-name RequestGroup StructureDefinition. That makes raw instances, generated types, canonical URLs, profile references, REST routes, and search bases incompatible without a resource-level transform. FMM 2 softens the standards burden, but the blast radius still warrants explicit transition guidance or alias review.

findingConsiderations.title: action.relatedAction.actionId was renamed to targetId
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a narrow same-type, same-cardinality rename from required `actionId` to required `targetId`. It does not drive the resource migration, but it is one of the clearest low-cost-to-preserve breaks: retaining the old wire name and clarifying its prose would likely have met the same goal with much less compatibility cost.

findingConsiderations.title: reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into reason CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard old-valid/new-invalid path change and reason content can affect clinical justification and auditability. Still, the R6 CodeableReference model directly addresses the old concept-or-reference split, and keeping both old arrays plus the unified field would create duplicate representations and ordering/precedence rules. It matters for migration tests but is less standards-actionable than the identity and `actionId` rename.

findingConsiderations.title: action.participant changed from direct Reference to participant backbone with actor[x]
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Participant migration is safety/business relevant because performer assignment can change workflow execution. The R4 direct Reference array must be wrapped as R6 participant.actorReference, while R6 supports richer role/function/canonical actor semantics. This is real migration work, but the richer model makes a simple base-compatible preservation less clean.

findingConsiderations.title: Required status and intent value sets add R6-only codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This does not reject old R4 codes because R6 retains them, so it is not a forward hard instance break. It still matters because status and intent are required modifier elements; R6-only values need explicit enum, state-machine, and R6-to-R4 mapping policy.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds multiple root/action orchestration fields not present in R4 RequestGroup
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These optional R6 capabilities create down-conversion and retention-policy chores, especially in safety-sensitive orchestration, but they do not make old R4 RequestGroup content invalid after the identity and element transforms. They should not inflate the R4-to-R6 compatibility conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: action.definition[x] was added and rqg-1 now allows exactly one of resource, action, or definition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The changed invariant preserves the old R4 cases where exactly one of resource or nested action exists. Definition-only R6 actions need a reverse-conversion policy, but this is additive for forward R4-to-R6 migration and does not argue for avoiding the resource remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a direct RequestGroup API concern because old queries such as RequestGroup patient searches no longer have the same R6 base endpoint. It reinforces the need for endpoint/search migration guidance and possibly transition aliases, but the root cause is the resource replacement rather than an independent search design issue.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The missing RequestGroup endpoint affects generic clients and conformance tooling that derive route inventories from the base CapabilityStatement. This is derivative of the resource lifecycle decision, but explicit replacement metadata or legacy endpoint guidance would materially reduce migration surprises.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may affect implementations that validate migrated RequestGroup/RequestOrchestration instances, but they are not RequestGroup-specific and should not be counted as resource-level RequestGroup breaks.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or verify an explicit RequestGroup-to-RequestOrchestration migration map covering resourceType, canonical/profile URLs, stored type discriminators, REST routes, search parameters, `reason`, `participant`, `relatedAction`, and status/intent terminology.

Standards reviewers should consider low-cost transition compatibility for the top-level resource/API identity and for `relatedAction.actionId`, where the break appears mostly to be naming rather than a substantive model change.

For production migration, add round-trip and validation tests for reason concept/reference splits, participant actor wrapping, nested related actions, RequestGroup search/endpoint migration, and R6-only modifier codes.

Define an R6-to-R4 retention policy for optional R6 orchestration fields such as goals, action definitions, input/output, location, dynamic values, transforms, RelativeTime, and new request status/intent codes.

caveats: No official HL7 migration guide, ConceptMap, rendered diff, or ballot rationale was supplied for RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration.
The review uses R4 FMM/status as the compatibility baseline; R6 ballot maturity does not increase the burden for breaking R4 consumers.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, not as RequestGroup-specific direct behavior findings.
